processing: Little is recorded for this strain; Dancong in general is withered, tossed for partial oxidation, fixed, rolled and dried.
harvest_season: Usually spring, as with most Fenghuang Dancong.
appearance_dry: Typically tight, straight, dark brown strips with an oily sheen, as is usual for the gardenia-aroma group.
appearance_liquor: Bright orange-yellow, typical of gardenia-aroma Dancong.
appearance_wet: Typically thick leaves with reddened edges, as with other tossed Dancong.
taste_profile: Listed among strains with a natural gardenia scent; the group usually gives a high floral nose, a mellow fresh body and a strong sweet return.

brewing.notes: General Dancong advice: plenty of leaf, hot water, quick pours.

vintage_note: Little is known about how this strain is sold under its own name. Dancong as a class goes by harvest year and season, usually fresh spring tea or tea rested a year or two after roasting.
description:
Zong Suo Xie is a Fenghuang Dancong strain listed among the seven gardenia-scented strains of the Huang Zhi Xiang group and named as a representative strain of the Song Zhong line.

No method specific to it is on record. Expect ordinary Dancong handling: withering, tossing, fixing, rolling and drying.

Its group is known for a high gardenia aroma, a mellow fresh body and a persistent sweet return. No detailed tasting notes for this strain alone are known, so taste it with that as a guide rather than a promise.

The spelling varies, and the name is rare on the market. If you find it, compare it with a standard Huang Zhi Xiang, the clearest way to learn what it adds.
history: Little is documented. Chinese writing on Dancong lists it in the gardenia aroma group, but its origin, the meaning of the name and who first selected it are not clearly recorded.
